title: Stage 4 placement and platform policy seams
purpose: Define connection-start placement and platform-capability seams while keeping route ownership, endpoint I/O, buffer ownership, lifecycle, and deterministic fallback authoritative.
scope: This checkpoint specifies connection_shard_placement and application_datagram_batch_transport as independent Stage 4 axes. Placement retains immutable connection-start routing. Datagram transport retains the current capability-gated segmented path and one-way client pressure promotion, adds ordinary_datagrams as the conservative value, and makes capability fallback, forcing, observe-only, shadow, unified evidence, and rollback explicit. Performance measurement and active behavior remain unauthorized.
context: The retained host assigns a sequential connection handle by modulo shard count. The retained transport uses Windows UDP_SEND_MSG_SIZE only after an exact socket capability probe, with a server path that batches whenever capable and a client path that promotes one way to ordinary sends under sustained distinct-stream pressure. Neither axis uses topology, workload, host, peer, URL, payload constants, requested concurrency, or application identity as controller input.

requirements.title: Force bounded connection-start shard placement without weakening route ownership
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST expose the connection_shard_placement axis with the closed legacy_current and bounded_power_of_two_choices values; preserve sequential-handle modulo shard-count assignment under legacy_current; make bounded_power_of_two_choices compare the legacy shard with exactly one deterministic distinct alternate using bounded active-connection counts and select the lower count with the legacy shard as the deterministic tie break; decide exactly once during successful connection registration and latch the applied shard for the connection lifetime; support disabled, observe-only, shadow, forced-legacy, and forced-bounded-choice operation with forced, recommended, selected, and applied identities distinct; make valid shard bounds, unique runtime and handle ownership, route insertion, failed-registration rollback, unregister accounting, lifecycle, shutdown, endpoint routing, timer ownership, packet routing, cancellation, disposal, recovery, congestion, pacing, flow control, packet size, queue, and buffer limits authoritative under every forced value; handle missing, stale, saturated, contradictory, invalid, out-of-domain, lifecycle, and single-shard input with bounded reasons and legacy fallback; publish the immutable connection-start decision into every unified epoch with exact connection identity and reject a changed latch; reject simultaneous behavior-distinct campaign forcing of adjacent axes; independently prove force-legacy rollback; exclude scenario, workload, payload constants, requested concurrency, peer, URL, host, and application identity from controller inputs; and keep migration, active_internal, and production selection unavailable.
notes: bounded_power_of_two_choices is a reviewed mechanism value, not a performance-derived claim.
Connection migration, topology-aware placement, measurement, active_internal, and production activation remain outside this requirement.

requirements.title: Force capability-gated application datagram transport without weakening endpoint safety
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST expose the application_datagram_batch_transport axis with the closed legacy_current, segmented_batch, and ordinary_datagrams values; preserve the current capability-gated server batching and one-way client pressure-promotion behavior under legacy_current; treat ordinary_datagrams as the distinct conservative implementation; support disabled, observe-only, shadow, forced-legacy, forced-segmented, and forced-ordinary operation with forced, recommended, selected, and applied identities distinct; decide at each application-send turn while latching legacy client promotion for the connection lifetime and socket capability for one monotonic capability epoch; make platform, address-family, socket-probe, custom-sender, endpoint, packet-size, segmentation, source-address, ECN, ownership, partial-send, cancellation, disposal, shutdown, recovery, congestion, pacing, flow-control, queue, and buffer guards authoritative under every forced value; fall back to ordinary datagrams for unavailable capability or missing, stale, saturated, contradictory, invalid, out-of-domain, and lifecycle input with bounded reasons; publish configured identity, capability, decisions, socket-call, datagram, segment, submitted-byte, accepted-byte, failure, partial-send, and lifecycle outcomes in every unified epoch; reject simultaneous behavior-distinct forcing and mismatched connection-local configuration; independently prove force-legacy rollback; exclude scenario, workload, payload constants, requested concurrency, peer, URL, host, and application identity from controller inputs; and keep performance selection, active_internal, and production activation unavailable.
notes: segmented_batch is capability-gated and never claims support on a platform, address family, socket, or sender where the probe is unavailable.
The current pressure threshold is preserved only as legacy behavior and is not tuned or promoted by this requirement.
